edits.target: ## Match theorem claims to the exact setup
edits.content:
- When an option adds an extension, classification, stronger structural assertion, or proposed exception to a base claim, establish each added clause under the exact hypotheses; do not import a vaguely related result. A result for a restricted class does not establish the broader claim, and symmetry or a dimension count alone does not establish a classification or single-orbit property.
- For time-dependent estimates, distinguish a bound on each fixed interval [0,T] with a constant C_T from one bound valid for all t ≥ 0 with a constant independent of the time horizon. Finite-horizon control does not imply global-in-time uniformity.

- Treat each option as a literal conjunction: verify every range, endpoint, constant, and added assertion independently. Do not supply omitted qualifiers from context, replace a printed bound with a customary convention, or accept a whole option because one clause is true. In particular, an upper bound does not establish a lower bound or an asymptotic equivalence.
- For a parametrized operation, derive its effect using the stated convention before comparing factors or divisibility conditions; wording alone does not determine whether the relevant quantity is the parameter or a multiple of it.

edits.target: - Preserve the exact form of asymptotic assertions: note cutoffs, the order of iterated limits, and whether the claim uses a limit or limsup. Do not silently replace a truncated approximation with convergence to a full series.
edits.content: - Interpret limit operators literally: `limsup` as t approaches T from below equals negative infinity means h(t) tends to negative infinity, while `liminf` equaling negative infinity only guarantees arbitrarily late values arbitrarily negative. Do not interchange them unless the hypotheses establish the needed convergence or monotonicity.

edits.target: - Preserve the exact form of asymptotic assertions: note cutoffs, the order of iterated limits, and whether the claim uses a limit or limsup. Do not silently replace a truncated approximation with convergence to a full series.
edits.content: - Keep exponent bounds distinct from endpoint power bounds: a statement such as liminf(log A_N / log N) ≥ α gives A_N ≥ N^(α−δ) eventually for every δ > 0, but does not by itself give A_N ≥ cN^α for a fixed c > 0. The latter does imply the exponent bound.

edits.target: - Before using a special case or counterexample to reject a claim, verify that it satisfies every structural assumption in the question, such as nondegeneracy, regularity, parameter restrictions, and the stated measure. A case that violates a hypothesis does not refute the claim.
edits.content: - Separate compactness of the stated parameter space from compactness of additional data: a convergent subsequence of structural parameters alone does not establish convergence of metrics or preservation of a geometric property in the limit.

edits.target: - Translate each option into its logical form before comparing it. Track quantifier order and dependencies: “for every target, there exists a witness” differs from one witness working for every target, and a constant that may depend on a parameter differs from a uniform constant. Distinguish all parameter values from sufficiently large values, and a whole class from a restricted subclass.
edits.content: - For a finite list of candidate limits, almost-sure convergence to one member of the list does not imply that each member occurs with positive probability. Treat a claim that every listed limit has positive probability, and any eventual-membership condition attached to it, as additional assertions to verify.
